en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) and the Dyad of Mental Association (Cittasampayuttaduka)
Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, a state that is neither-wholesome-nor-unwholesome and not associated with consciousness arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, a state that is unwholesome and not associated with consciousness arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, a state that is indeterminate...

A state not associated with consciousness arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, there arise states that are unwholesome, not associated with consciousness, and neither-defined-nor-undefined, and states that are neither-defined-nor-undefined and not associated with consciousness, by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, there arises a state that is unwholesome and not associated with consciousness... [and so forth].
Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, there arises a state that is not wholesome and not associated with consciousness... [and so forth].
And unwholesome states that are not associated with consciousness arise by way of root condition … five.
Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness, an unwholesome state that is not associated with consciousness arises by way of root condition … five.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with consciousness, a non-wholesome state that is not associated with consciousness arises … [five].
By way of root condition: dependent on an indeterminate state associated with consciousness, there arises an unwholesome state not associated with consciousness by way of root condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with consciousness, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor associated with consciousness, and states that are neither unwholesome nor associated with consciousness, by way of root condition.
... three. (Abbreviated. With root-cause condition there are thirteen; with object condition nine ... pe ... with resultant condition three ... pe ... with non-disappearance condition thirteen.
With mind-dissociated [condition] there are three; with root-cause condition there are three ... pe ... with non-disappearance condition three.
